- Work must land on branch `feature/story-03-user-agent-authentication`. Do not modify Story 01 / 02 files unless authentication truly requires it (only expected touches: `Program.cs`, `AppDbContext.cs`, `AppRouter.tsx`, `httpClient.ts`, `useAppStore.ts`, `en.json`/`ar.json`).

---

## Story Goal

Introduce internal Agent/User authentication as the first real domain slice of the CRM:

1. Persistable `User` entity with hashed password, first EF Core migration checked in.
2. `POST /api/auth/login` returns a bearer JWT on valid credentials, `401` on invalid.
3. JWT bearer authentication middleware registered; at least one protected route (`GET /api/auth/me`) returns `401` when unauthenticated and `200` with the current user when authenticated.
4. `GET /api/health` stays anonymous and unchanged (Story 01 contract).
5. Frontend login screen at `/login` that authenticates against the new endpoint, persists the token client-side (same `zustand/persist` pattern as `language`), attaches it to all subsequent Axios requests, and gates `HomePage` behind an auth guard.
6. Logout clears session and returns to `/login`. Session survives reload.
7. Login screen uses `PageContainer`, Tailwind conventions, `react-i18next` (EN + AR), RTL-aware layout — visually consistent with `HomePage`.

**Not in scope:** roles/permissions, password reset, MFA, SSO, customer-facing auth, audit logging, ticket/customer domain, ASP.NET Identity framework, refresh tokens.

**Create file: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Domain/User.cs`**

namespace CustomerSupportCrm.Api.Domain;

public class User
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public string Email { get; set; } = string.Empty;   // stored lower-case

**Create file: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Auth/JwtTokenService.cs`**

- Constructor takes `IConfiguration`.
- `string IssueToken(User user, out DateTime expiresAtUtc)` builds a `JwtSecurityToken` with claims `sub=User.Id`, `email=User.Email`, `name=User.DisplayName`, signed with `HmacSha256` using `Jwt:SigningKey` (UTF-8 bytes). Issuer/Audience from config. Expiry = `DateTime.UtcNow + Jwt:ExpiryMinutes`. Return the encoded token via `JwtSecurityTokenHandler().WriteToken(...)`.

### 6 — `AuthController`

**Create file: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Controllers/AuthController.cs`**

Route: `[Route("api/[controller]")]` (matches `HealthController` convention on `HealthController.cs:6`).

Endpoints:

- `[HttpPost("login")] [AllowAnonymous]` → accepts `LoginRequest`.
  - Trim + lower-case email.
  - Load user by email from `AppDbContext.Users`.
  - If null → `return Unauthorized(new { error = "invalid_credentials" });`.
  - `PasswordHasher<User>.VerifyHashedPassword(user, user.PasswordHash, request.Password)` — if `Failed` → same 401.
  - Otherwise issue JWT and return `LoginResponse`.
- `[HttpGet("me")] [Authorize]` → reads `User.FindFirst("sub")`, loads by id, returns `MeResponse`. Returns `401` implicitly when unauthenticated (thanks to `[Authorize]`).

Match the response style used at `HealthController.cs:12` (`Ok(new { ... })`).

### 7 — Wire authentication into `Program.cs`

**File: `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Program.cs`** (lines 1–33)

- Add `using` lines for `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer`, `Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens`, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity`, `CustomerSupportCrm.Api.Domain`, `CustomerSupportCrm.Api.Auth`.
- After `AddSwaggerGen()` (line 8), add:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddSingleton<PasswordHasher<User>>();
builder.Services.AddSingleton<JwtTokenService>();

var jwt = builder.Configuration.GetSection("Jwt");
builder.Services
    .AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
    .AddJwtBearer(options =>
    {
        options.TokenValidationParameters = new TokenValidationParameters
        {
            ValidateIssuer = true,
            ValidateAudience = true,
            ValidateLifetime = true,
            ValidateIssuerSigningKey = true,
            ValidIssuer = jwt["Issuer"],
            ValidAudience = jwt["Audience"],
            IssuerSigningKey = new SymmetricSecurityKey(
                System.Text.Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(jwt["SigningKey"] ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Jwt:SigningKey missing"))),
        };
    });
builder.Services.AddAuthorization();
```

- Between `app.UseCors("Frontend");` (line 30) and `app.MapControllers();` (line 31), insert:

```csharp
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();
```

## Frontend Tasks

### 9 — Auth store

**Create file: `frontend/src/store/useAuthStore.ts`**

Follow the shape of `useAppStore.ts` (lines 1–27) exactly:

```ts
import { create } from 'zustand';
import { persist, createJSONStorage } from 'zustand/middleware';

export interface AuthUser {
  email: string;
  displayName: string;
}

interface AuthState {
  token: string | null;
  user: AuthUser | null;
  expiresAtUtc: string | null;
  setSession: (payload: { token: string; user: AuthUser; expiresAtUtc: string }) => void;
  clearSession: () => void;
  isAuthenticated: () => boolean;
}

export const useAuthStore = create<AuthState>()(
  persist(
    (set, get) => ({
      token: null,
      user: null,
      expiresAtUtc: null,
      setSession: ({ token, user, expiresAtUtc }) => set({ token, user, expiresAtUtc }),
      clearSession: () => set({ token: null, user: null, expiresAtUtc: null }),
      isAuthenticated: () => {
        const { token, expiresAtUtc } = get();
        if (!token || !expiresAtUtc) return false;
        return new Date(expiresAtUtc).getTime() > Date.now();
      },
    }),
    {
      name: 'cscrm-auth-store',
      storage: createJSONStorage(() => localStorage),
      partialize: (state) => ({ token: state.token, user: state.user, expiresAtUtc: state.expiresAtUtc }),
    },
  ),
);
```

**Do not** touch `useAppStore.ts` — its `appName`/`language` state is Story 01/02 contract.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty email or password** — `LoginPage.tsx` blocks submit (HTML `required` + a JS guard); backend still validates and returns `401` if it somehow arrives. Never a 500.
- **Wrong password** — `AuthController.Login` returns `401` with `{ "error": "invalid_credentials" }`. Frontend shows `auth.errors.invalidCredentials`; **do not** leak whether the email exists.
- **Unknown email** — Same `401` / same client message (no user enumeration).
- **Expired token** — `useAuthStore.isAuthenticated()` returns `false` when `expiresAtUtc` has passed; `RequireAuth` redirects to `/login`. Server-side `ValidateLifetime = true` (task 7) also rejects.
- **Token stripped or corrupted in `localStorage`** — `persist` rehydration yields `token=null` / expired; treated as logged-out. No crash on load.
- **Backend down or CORS misconfig** — Axios throws; login screen shows `auth.errors.network`. `httpClient.ts` `baseURL` still resolves from `VITE_API_BASE_URL`.
- **401 on any request post-login** — response interceptor in `httpClient.ts` (task 10) clears the session; next navigation triggers `RequireAuth` → `/login`.
- **Reload while logged in** — `zustand/persist` rehydrates from `cscrm-auth-store` in `localStorage`, mirroring how `cscrm-app-store` rehydrates `language` (see `useAppStore.ts:22`). User stays on `/`.
- **RTL language selected on login screen** — Login layout uses the same logical spacing utilities as `HomePage.tsx`; no `ml-/mr-` directional utilities that would break Arabic.
- **`GET /api/health` regression risk** — `HealthController.cs` has no `[Authorize]` and this story adds none. Regression is caught by the smoke test in the verification section.
- **First-time DB with empty `Users`** — Development seed (task 8) inserts `admin@example.com`. Non-Development environments do **not** seed; login will fail until a user is inserted out-of-band. Document this in a code comment inside `SeedData.cs`.
- **Missing `Jwt:SigningKey`** — `Program.cs` throws `InvalidOperationException` at startup so misconfiguration fails loudly, not silently.
- **Concurrent logins from same browser tab** — `setSession` is a single atomic Zustand update; last one wins.
- **Unicode in email** — Store lower-cased using `String.ToLowerInvariant()`; unique index enforces uniqueness. No normalization of the local part beyond case-folding.

## Migration / Rollback

- **Applying:** `dotnet ef database update` from `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/` creates the `Users` table with `Id` PK and unique index on `Email`.
- **Rolling back the DB:** `dotnet ef database update 0` reverses the migration, then `dotnet ef migrations remove` deletes the generated files if the migration is being replaced. Revert code changes in `AppDbContext.cs`, `Program.cs`, delete `Domain/User.cs`, `Auth/`, `Controllers/AuthController.cs`, and the migration folder.
- **Half-applied risk:** If code is deployed without running the migration, `POST /api/auth/login` will throw a SQL error on missing `Users` table. Mitigation: developers must run `database update` before hitting `/login`; document in the PR.
- **Rollback on frontend:** Reverting `AppRouter.tsx` restores the pre-auth single-route behavior; `useAuthStore` file can be deleted; `httpClient.ts` reverts to its 10-line original. No user data is lost because auth state lives only in `localStorage`.
